faq.q: Why are LED bulbs better than old bulbs?
faq.a: An LED bulb gives the same light for about a fifth of the electricity, lasts many times longer and runs much cooler. Over its life it saves far more than it costs.
asks: Should I switch to LED bulbs?

faq.a: They get warm but not scorching. The heat collects in the base, which is why LED bulbs have metal or ridged bases to carry it away.
asks: Why is the bottom of an LED bulb warm?

faq.q: How long does an LED bulb last?
faq.a: A good LED bulb is rated for around 15,000 to 25,000 hours, compared with about 1,000 hours for a filament bulb. Used a few hours a day, that is well over ten years.
asks: How many hours does an LED last?

faq.q: Why does an LED bulb have electronics in its base?
faq.a: Mains electricity is high-voltage alternating current, but LEDs need a small, steady direct current. A tiny driver circuit in the base converts it.
asks: What is the driver in an LED bulb?

faq.q: Why do filament bulbs waste so much energy?
faq.a: A filament has to be white-hot to glow, and hot things send out most of their energy as invisible infrared heat, so only about 5 percent becomes visible light.

facts: An LED bulb that replaces a 60 watt filament bulb typically uses about 8 to 10 watts.
A filament bulb typically lasts about 1,000 hours.
